cands.bio: Attorney and Democrat who has represented New Jersey in the U.S. House since 1988. Earlier served on the Long Branch City Council (1982–1988) and in the New Jersey State Senate. Former chair and current ranking member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee.

endorsements.text: His campaign site lists endorsements from the Transport Workers Union of America, Middlesex County Democratic Organization, NJEA PAC, SEIU 32BJ, LCV Action Fund, CWA, National Wildlife Federation, Planned Parenthood Action Fund and the NJ State Policemen's Benevolent Association.
Ballotpedia lists New Jersey Citizen Action and Humane World Action Fund among his 2026 endorsements.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by Pallone on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on institutional or foreign land buyers, growth limits and land conservation, gun laws, police pay and pensions, or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. We found no documented controversies in the pages we reviewed. The pages gave no date for when his family moved to the area, but he was born and raised in Long Branch.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

cands.name: Hillary Herzig

money.note: Individuals gave $7,054; PAC money $0; candidate's own money $4,712. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Republican candidate for U.S. House in New Jersey's 6th District. She lists a 2010–2025 federal civil service career: Army intelligence security, Veterans Administration, USDA-APHIS and USCIS. Earlier she was executive assistant to the Key West police chief. Also an artist, author and military spouse. Has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: In her Ballotpedia survey she lists endorsements from the Monmouth County Republican Committee, Middlesex County Republican Organization, New Jersey Young Republican Federation and New Jersey Federation of Republican Women. Ballotpedia says it did not independently identify any endorsements.

cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace or the exact date she returned to New Jersey beyond 2022. We found no record of elected office, bills, or official actions, so there is nothing showing what she has done in office. We found no stated position on data centers, development limits, or New Jersey land purchases by investors, foreign buyers or out-of-state buyers. We found nothing on H-1B visas or on state cooperation with immigration enforcement; her site only says she supports legal immigration and national sovereignty. We found no stated position on abortion, and none on red-flag laws, suppressors or similar gun rules beyond a general statement supporting Second Amendment rights. We found no teacher-pay proposal and no pledge to refuse particular kinds of donations. No news coverage or controversies were found in the pages available. Her employment history comes from her own campaign site and was not confirmed by outside records.

local.label: Roots 90: She says she was raised in Middletown, attended New Jersey schools, and returned in 2022 to raise her family in Oceanport; her birthplace is not stated in the pages found.

score.why: Raised $11.8k, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Self-reported career civil servant 2010–2025: executive assistant to the Key West police chief, Army intelligence security representative, Defense Department dependent-school instructor, VA financial analyst, USDA-APHIS benefits technician, and USCIS asylum mission support and personnel security specialist. Also an artist and business owner. She has held no elected office.
qual.why: Agency work in security, benefits and immigration processing is relevant to oversight and constituent service, but the roles listed are not senior policy, legislative or budget-authority positions and she has no legislative or elected experience. This places her in the middle range. The employment history comes from her own campaign site and was not independently verified.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Her campaign site says she will fight for lower property taxes and a reduced cost of living. It gives no specific homestead-tax proposal.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site says families deserve the freedom to choose the best learning environment for their children. She also lists school choice and homeschooling among her passions in her Ballotpedia survey. She does not mention teacher pay.

second-amendment.evidence: In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey she lists second amendment rights and limits on government surveillance among her policy priorities. She gives no specific proposals.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site lists 'Law and Order' as a priority, saying every family deserves safe streets and secure communities. It cites her work with the Key West Police Department. It also says she would limit law-enforcement technology used to spy on Americans.
